blocks.content: To locate any place precisely on the globe, we need lines of reference running from the North Pole to the South Pole called meridians of longitude.

rows: Parallel circles running East to West
Varies; decreases from Equator to Poles
Determining location East/West and time zones

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Latitudes alone are insufficient to pinpoint an exact place, necessitating vertical lines of reference.
Meridians of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole and are all equal in length.
The Prime Meridian (0°) passes through Greenwich, London, dividing the Earth into Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
Earth rotates 15° every hour, which creates a 4-minute time difference for every 1° of longitude.
A uniform Standard Meridian is adopted by countries to establish a single standard time and avoid local time confusion.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated from the 82°30' E meridian passing through Mirzapur (UP), placing it 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
The 180° East and 180° West meridians meet on the exact same line, forming the International Date Line.
The distance between meridians of longitude is maximum at the Equator and decreases to zero at the Poles.
